summary:
Your messages queue is clear: all 7 refill messages are closed under refill protocol RBC-RX-05. Three results that came in while I worked changed decisions I had already made. As a result, none of the three patients got a lisinopril refill, and all three lisinopril requests now need your review.

**Frank Odum (pt-0027), lisinopril 10 mg**
- First decision: his August outside potassium of 5.9 was on a damaged (hemolyzed) sample, so it didn't count. I renewed lisinopril for 90 days (mr-t0001) based on his 1/20 potassium of 4.5, and ordered a repeat BMP (sr-t0002).
- Then a new St. Brigid report arrived (doc-00601): BMP drawn 10/20 on a good sample, potassium 5.8. I cancelled mr-t0001 before anything was dispensed.
- Urgent task to you: task-t0020. His hernia repair is scheduled for 11/12.

**Samuel Price (pt-0030), lisinopril 20 mg and metformin 1000 mg twice daily**
- Metformin: the patient asked once and the pharmacy asked twice; I handled them as one request. Renewed for 90 days with 1 refill (mr-t0004). His eGFR is 58 and his HbA1c was 7.1% on 8/19 (outside lab).
- Lisinopril: first renewed for 90 days (mr-t0003). Then the lab corrected his 10/6 creatinine from 1.36 to 1.49. That is 35% above his 1.10 baseline, 18 days after the dose increase, so the protocol treats it like a potassium of 5.5 or higher. I cancelled mr-t0003.
- The corrected eGFR (58) doesn't change the metformin decision.
- Urgent task to you: task-t0021.

**Marcus Webb (pt-0031), lisinopril 10 mg and metformin 500 mg twice daily**
- Metformin: renewed for 90 days with 1 refill (mr-t0007). His most recent valid eGFR is 92; the 10/14 eGFR of 39 was marked entered in error (mislabelled sample). HbA1c was 6.9% on 9/28.
- Lisinopril: his last BMP was over 12 months old, so I first sent a 30-day supply with no refills (mr-t0005) and ordered a BMP (sr-t0006).
- Then a BMP drawn 10/22 came back with potassium 5.8 (obs-06001). I cancelled mr-t0005.
- Urgent task to you: task-t0022.

**Things to know**
- All three patients' previous lisinopril orders (mr-00283, mr-00295, mr-00297) were stopped when I placed the replacements, and they stay stopped. No new lisinopril orders are in place.
- Each patient got a first reply and then a corrected message saying the lisinopril was not sent and you will contact them. For Mr. Odum and Mr. Webb the correction also covers warning symptoms (weakness, palpitations, chest discomfort) and when to seek urgent care.
- In my correction to Mr. Webb I told him he doesn't need the new blood test for now, because he had one on 10/22. The BMP order itself (sr-t0006) is still active, since I can't cancel lab orders. Please cancel it or tell him otherwise.
- Mr. Odum's repeat BMP order (sr-t0002) is also still active.
- I wrote a note in each chart (doc-t0027, doc-t0028, doc-t0029) explaining the first decision and why it was corrected.
- I left the three new results (inbox-a0001, inbox-a0002, inbox-a0004) and the rest of your results queue open for you to review.
